category_title: At-risk students who resist connecting home and school contexts
scenario_title: Whole-group classroom discussion about social issues
minimal_context: The student is participating in a whole-group classroom discussion about rules in society and the topic of bullying.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Today we are discussing rules in the classroom and in society. The topic of bullying came up. What are some examples of bullying?

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Can you tell me a bit more about that?

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Does anyone have any other examples from outside of school?

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Today we are discussing rules in the classroom and in society. The topic of bullying came up. What are some examples of bullying?

STUDENT: Teasing.

TUTOR: Can you tell me a bit more about that?

STUDENT: Just teasing. That's it.

TUTOR: Does anyone have any other examples from outside of school?

STUDENT: Blackmailing. Effects cause suicide.

task.content: Classroom discussion about rules in the classroom and society during the summer school session, specifically the topic of bullying

context.environment: 8-week summer school English Language Arts program

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When the teacher asked for some examples of bullying
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Students merely listed some responses. They did not elaborate

behavior_patterns.condition: On the rare occasions when the students brought their outside of school lives into the class discussion
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: They listed an event or object with little, if any, elaboration, clearly mimicking their in-class videos

The students rarely initiated a contribution to class discussions that included relationships or events from their lives outside of school. Any connection to their lives outside of school was rare and minimally expressed
